chunks: Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a dog that escaped and whose owner did not release it, yet it hunted, and its owner caught up with it after it had killed the prey. May he eat from it?
So he said: “No. If it hunted while he had mentioned Allah's name, then let him eat. But if it hunted and he did not mention Allah's name, then let him not eat. And it is from that which…”
"you have trained among the hunting animals, training them as hounds"

key_terms.أَفْلَتَ: escaped or got loose without deliberate release
key_terms.الْجَوَارِحِ: trained hunting animals or beasts of prey
key_terms.سَمَّى: mentioned the name of Allah before the hunt
key_terms.كَلْبٍ: a hunting dog involved in catching prey
key_terms.مُكَلِّبِينَ: training animals for hunting, especially as hounds

ai.seo_question: Can prey killed by a hunting dog that escaped be eaten in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about prey caught by a hunting dog that escaped on its own rather than being deliberately released. The ruling turns on the mention of Allah's name, and the Imam عليه السلام supports the legal point by citing the Qur'anic wording about trained hunting animals.
